scope: First full nine-object EN-SCI, English correctness and ZHEN text review against the exact D020-approved current Chinese baseline
summary: All nine English objects preserve the approved Chinese meaning and conditions. Fixed isolated-conductor geometry/environment and the unchanged potential reference are retained; the historical approximate 9 times 10^11 conversion, slightly-over-13 solar-radius comparison and 709-microfarad estimate remain qualified. The electrostatic capacitance centimeter is distinguished from length, and relative permittivity remains dimensionless while vacuum permittivity is not made size-dependent. No necessary correction was found.

objectReview.assessment: Charge-change/potential-change relation and the isolated conductor's fixed shape, surrounding medium and external-conductor positions are explicit; (8-33) is retained.

Adding 1 coulomb and raising potential by 1 volt under the stated conditions defines the farad. Before/after potentials use the same reference point. The strong-emphasis delimiters surround the intended definition correctly.
The historical electrostatic centimeter is defined from an isolated sphere with radius 1 centimeter in vacuum using (8-35). The text expressly distinguishes the capacitance unit from a length.
Charge/potential unit conversion and the original approximate values are retained; equality signs are explicitly qualified as results under those approximations.

The complete conversion chain preserves 1/1, (3 times 10^9)/(1/300), and 9 times 10^11, together with charge/potential unit order. Centimeters here remains the capacitance-unit name established in object 3, not physical conductor length.

The vacuum isolated-sphere scale, slightly more than 13 solar radii, microfarad 10^-6 and picofarad 10^-12 are preserved. Earth's 709 microfarads is an original approximate model estimate with other conductors excluded, not an exact environment-independent value.
The isolated conducting sphere is surrounded by a homogeneous, linear, isotropic medium. The (8-34) relation and vacuum-permittivity subject are retained within that model.
Rearrangement retains original notation and epsilon_0=C/(4 pi epsilon r), including all mathematical tokens.

C is sphere capacitance, r is radius, and the denominator's relative permittivity is dimensionless. Farad per meter is derived as the unit of vacuum permittivity, with an explicit statement that vacuum permittivity does not change with sphere size.
